memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Routine follow‑up of type 2 diabetes, osteoarthritis knee and IBS. Reports stable knee pain, occasional abdominal bloating, good adherence to meds. EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.6 (obese). Joints: mild tenderness bilateral knees, no effusion. Abdomen soft, non‑tender. IMPRESSION: 1) Type 2 diabetes, HbA1c pending. 2) Osteoarthritis knees, overweight. 3) IBS, controlled. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue metformin 500 mg BD, glimepiride 1 mg OD ac, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD. Paracetamol 650 mg SOS for knee pain, topical diclofenac gel BD, calcium‑vit D3 OD. Mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Order fasting lipid profile, HbA1c, fasting glucose, urine ACR, serum vitamin D, CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA. Weight‑bearing X‑ray both knees. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, worsening knee swelling, bloody stools, severe abdominal pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Weight‑bearing anteroposterior X‑ray of both knees. Findings: Mild joint space narrowing medially, osteophyte formation at tibial plateaus, no significant effusion or fracture. Impression: Early osteoarthritis changes bilaterally, consistent with clinical symptoms.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Review of labs and knee X‑ray; reports increased fasting glucose and mild knee discomfort on stairs. EXAMINATION: BP 142/90 mmHg, weight 79 kg, BMI 28.0 (obese). Knees: mild tenderness, crepitus, no warmth. Abdomen: soft, no masses. IMPRESSION: 1) Type 2 diabetes – HbA1c 7.8% indicates suboptimal control. 2) Osteoarthritis knees – radiographic early changes. 3) Vitamin D deficiency. 4) Mild dyslipidemia. ARRANGEMENTS: Increase metformin to 500 mg TID. Add insulin glargine 10 units at bedtime, titrate. Continue glimepiride, sitagliptin, empagliflozin. Start vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Advise weight reduction, low‑impact exercise. Repeat HbA1c in 3 months. Return if: polyuria, polydipsia, unexplained weight loss, severe knee pain, swelling, fever.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to Dr S. Rao, Ophthalmology, Narayana Nethralaya, for dilated fundus examination to screen for diabetic retinopathy. Patient advised to bring recent HbA1c and BP records.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Ophthalmology report: Dilated fundus exam shows mild microaneurysms in temporal periphery, no macular edema, no proliferative changes. Recommend tight glycemic control and repeat exam in 12 months. No laser treatment needed now.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more tired lately and my knees hurt after long walks. Also my stomach feels upset after eating spicy food.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Follow‑up after patient‑reported fatigue and knee pain; reviews recent labs. EXAMINATION: BP 136/84 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 27.3 (overweight). Knees: mild tenderness, no effusion. Abdomen: soft, no distress. IMPRESSION: 1) Type 2 diabetes – HbA1c 7.2% (improved). 2) Osteoarthritis knees – stable. 3) Vitamin D 32 ng/mL (now sufficient). 4) IBS – symptoms diet‑related. ARRANGEMENTS: Continue metformin 500 mg TID, glimepiride 1 mg OD, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD, insulin glargine 8 units nightly (reduced). Keep vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Advise low‑impact aerobic activity, avoid high‑impact knee strain. Repeat HbA1c and lipid profile in 6 months. Return if: worsening fatigue, visual changes, chest pain, severe knee swelling, bloody stools.
